key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer combines improved solar-cell efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against ambient degradation.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to more efficient, environmentally stable hybrid Schottky solar cells on untextured silicon.
method: Benchmark planar trilayer cells against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and impermeable protective barrier.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days in ambient conditions, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract reports 75-day ambient stability, but does not establish long-term outdoor durability or manufacturing-scale reproducibility.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
